headlines.full_text: 'I was not going to let others die' - pilot of Flydubai flight describes cockpit attack by co-pilot Capt Smit Machchhar tells Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi he opened the cockpit door to let others in during the attack. The Indian pilot of the Flydubai plane who was stabbed by his co-pilot and opened the cockpit door to let others in has said he was determined not to let others die. Capt Smit Machchhar said he was on the floor and still being attacked when he realised the plane carrying more than 170 passengers was sinking and he had to do something. "I was lying on the floor injured but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside," he said in a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. "Others came in and also played a role [in controlling the situation]. I was of course fighting for my own life but at the same time I knew I was not going to let others die," he added. Flydubai's flight FZ1073, which was bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai early on Wednesday morning, plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey. It first sent an emergency signal to air traffic controllers before switching to code squawk 7500, which indicates hijacking. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told the media that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane. After fellow passengers overpowered the attacker, two reserve pilots, who were onboard, safely landed the plane at Tabuk Airport in north-western Saudi Arabia at 06:58 local time. Machchhar, who has been hailed as a "true hero" by Netanyahu, was taken to hospital in Tabuk before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition. Ne

headlines.full_text: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination' Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane". Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says investigations suggest the man who stabbed his fellow pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination". The Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely. Netanyahu told Fox News that it was looking "very likely" that the attacker, who he said was an Omani national, "was going to down the plane". Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) state news agency reports investigations have begun there to determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose". The Interior Ministry of Saudi Arabia - where the plane made an emergency landing - said that both the pilot and co-pilot had been sent back to the UAE on Thursday morning after medical teams had cleared them. UAE officials earlier claimed jurisdiction over the incident because the aircraft on which the attack took place is registered there and flies under its flag. Netanyahu told Fox that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question". headlines.full_text: Israeli reporter’s ‘verbal attack’ ends Ireland football news conference Israeli journalists asked coach Hallgrimsson about the Flydubai attack and alleged racist abuse by Ireland's players. Save Share Members of an Israeli media contingent heckled Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson’s news conference prior to the UEFA Nations League football match, causing it to end abruptly amid growing political tensions and protests against the fixture. During the media event on Saturday, an Israeli journalist asked Hallgrimsson about his views on an incident onboarda Flydubai flight to Israelearlier this week. According to the prosecutor general of the United Arab Emirates, the Flydubai co-pilot “attempted to carry out a terrorist act”, using an axe against the pilot to take over the aircraft’s controls. The plane carrying 174 passengers was on its way from the Dubai in the UAE to Tel Aviv in Israel on Wednesday when the copilot wounded Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who opened the cockpit door to seek help. The aircraft briefly plunged about 17,000 feet (5,180 metres) before it was brought back under control. The attacker was not officially identified, but media reports quoting unnamed sources said he was an Omani national, Hamam al-Hammami. “What do you say about the people that you support? headlines.full_text: Troubled Flydubai plane remains at Saudi airport for four days now The source found it difficult to say when the plane could possibly return MOSCOW, October 3. /TASS/. The plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv that made an emergency landing because of an internal personnel incident on board on September 30 has been at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia for a fourth day, a source in a Middle Eastern air traffic control service told TASS on Saturday. "The plane on board of which a cockpit incident occurred and which made an emergency landing en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv for that reason is still at the airport of Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk," the source said. On the day when that incident took place passengers from the troubled flight were taken to Tel Aviv on board another plane while the aircraft in question still stays where it landed, he recalled. The source found it difficult to say when the plane could possibly return. "It seems everything will depend on how the probe into the incident unfolds," he noted. On September 30, a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport following a security incident. On October 1, the Saudi Ministry of the Interior confirmed that the incident was caused by the stabbing of the flight captain by his co-pilot which left the two of them with injuries of varying severity. Both pilots departed for Abu Dhabi with an Emirati security escort once their condition had stabilized, while the other six crew members had earlier safely returned to Dubai, the Saudi ministry specified. Flydubai Flight FZ1073 sent a general emergency signal over Jordanian airspace, then a second indicating possible unlawful interference minutes later, according to flight-tracking website Flightradar24. The Boeing 737 sent the general emergency signal again before landing at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, the website said. The airport said it received a distress call from the aircraft at 8:44 a.m. local time requesting an emergency landing. Both the captain and co-pilot were wounded and taken to hospital. headlines.full_text: School protests send shivers down French government's spine A movement that started nearly two weeks ago has spread, and in France young people on the streets spells trouble, writes Hugh Schofield. It is a piece of wisdom that all French leaders take care to heed: young people on the street equals trouble. Since the student protests of May 1968 – memorably described by President De Gaulle aschienlit(bed defecation, in other words chaos) – every government has run scared of angry French youth. Why? Because youth movements are unpredictable and shapeless, often with no clear structure to negotiate with. Because when they protest, other groups join in. Also: because as they're young, the public tends to sympathise. And because if the police mess up and cause injury or worse, then the consequences are incalculable. And presidential elections are only months away. For all these reasons, whenla jeunesse en colère(angry youth) is at the barricades governments tread very carefully indeed. Right now, French teenagers are at the barricades and if they are not visibly angry (the mood is more excitement), they certainly have the government of President Emmanuel Macron in whatLe Mondecalled on Friday "the cold sweats". A movement that started nearly two weeks ago in the low-income Seine-Saint-Denis area of northern Paris has in the last few days spread across the country. Live: Fires lit on streets across France after student protests force hundreds of schools to close On Thursday – the high point so far – hundreds of lycées (where 15-18 year-olds finish their schooling) were being blockaded. headlines.full_text: Are Houthis making Pakistan nervous? Mecca pact tested as Saudis get hammered The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are testing the Mecca Agreement and delivering a reality check for Pakistan: any ambition of playing a greater role in West Asia also means inheriting the region’s conflicts, rivalries, and security challenges. The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia are testing the Mecca Agreement and delivering a reality check for Pakistan: any ambition of playing a greater role in West Asia also means inheriting the region’s conflicts, rivalries, and security challenges. The Mecca Agreement of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey rests on two mutually reinforcing pillars: first, it seeks to deter an attack on any member by making clear that an attack against one will be treated as an attack against all. Second, in case an attack occurs, it promises a collective response from the three members. Just like Nato,on which the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkey alliance is modelled, the logic is straightforward: the credibility of the promise of a collective response is what gives the deterrent its force. But the spiralling Saudi-Houthi conflict has now strained both pillars of the alliance. As the Houthis have hammered Saudi Arabia for weeks,the pact’s deterrence has failed to prevent the attacks, and the promise of a collective response is now being put to the test. And that raises a fundamental question: Are Pakistan and Turkey actually willing to follow through on their promises? Despite rhetoric from Defence Minister Khawaja Asif,who pledged to defend Saudi Arabia by “whatever means available”, Aishwaria Sonavane of the Takshashila Institution said that Pakistan faces significant political and military constraints to joining the fight. headlines.full_text: Brazil to hold first round of presidential election The vote will determine not only the country’s president for the next four years, but also state and Federal District governors RIO DE JANEIRO, October 4. /TASS/. Brazil will hold the first round of general elections. The vote will determine not only the country’s president for the next four years, but also state and Federal District governors. Voters will also elect an entirely new Chamber of Deputies and one-third of the Federal Senate, the lower and upper houses of Congress, respectively, as well as members of regional legislative assemblies. Brazil elects its president, governors and senators under a majority system, while federal and regional lawmakers are elected under a proportional system. If none of the candidates for executive office wins an absolute majority in the first round, a runoff will be held on October 25. Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which performs the functions of the country’s central election commission, has registered 12 candidates for president. According to the TSE, 158,745,502 citizens are eligible to vote. Voting is mandatory for all literate citizens aged 18 to 69, inclusive. Voting is optional for illiterate citizens, people aged 16 and 17, and those over 70. Polling stations will be open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time (11:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. GMT). Preliminary results will start coming in shortly after the polls close. The final results are usually available within a few hours thanks to the electronic voting system.

headlines.full_text: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality. To callBosnia and Herzegovinaa complicated country is an understatement. The country in the Balkan Peninsula divides its economic, administrative and political responsibilities between the multiethnic central government, the self-governing neutral Brcko district and two semi-autonomous entities that, for the most part, operate independently — the Muslim-Croat Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Serb-runRepublika Srpska. Both semi-autonomous entities are further split into several cantons and communities, home to mostly Bosniaks and Bosnian Croats in the central-western federation and Bosnian Serbs in Republika Srpska, to the north and east. This principle of ethnic nationalism is key to the country's central constitutional and political organization. The Bosnian constitution recognizes Bosniaks, who are predominantly Muslim, the largely Orthodox Bosnian Serbs and primarily Catholic Bosnian Croats as "constituent peoples" with equal rights. Today, the country has a population of around 3.1 million people. Around half are Bosniaks, while 31% are Serb and 15% are Croat. The rest of the inhabitants belong either to one of the 17 officially recognized minorities, like theRomaandJews, or chose not to identify with any ethnicity at the last official census. Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian are all recognized as official languages. Support for Merz’s party hits record low as AfD surges – poll Nationwide support for Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s CDU/CSU alliance has fallen to a historic low of 18%, according to a new poll
Read Full Article at RT.com Nationwide support for German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s CDU/CSU alliance has collapsed to a historic low following a series of defeats in regional elections, a new poll has suggested. The bloc’s popular backing stood at just 18%, its worst result in Germany’s postwar history, according to a survey conducted by the INSA polling institution on behalf of Bild. The poll put the right-wing Alternative for Germany (AfD) at 30%, its highest result since the party was established in 2013. It remains the most popular party in Germany by a wide margin, the poll suggested. The CDU/CSU’s junior coalition partners, the Social Democrats and the Greens are polling at 14% each, and the Left Party is at 10%. The survey was conducted between September 28 and October 2 among 1,202 eligible voters, with the results published on Saturday. Support for the CDU/CSU has fallen sharply since Merz took office as chancellor in May 2025. INSA put the bloc at around 30% shortly before he assumed the post, compared with 18% now. He has been imprisoned since August 2023 and faces multiple cases following his ousting in 2022. Islamabad:The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered on Tuesday that former Prime Minister Imran Khan ​be moved to a hospital from jail, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party ‌said, meeting a longstanding demand of his party and family, who had raised concerns about his health. Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been in jail since August ​2023, convicted in a string of cases that he ​says were politically driven following his ouster in 2022. A three-member Supreme Court bench, headed by Justice Shahid Wahid and comprising Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, issued the ruling on Imran's petition for his hospitalisation. His sons ⁠repeatedly expressed concern regarding his deteriorating health last year, with his ​lawyers saying he had lost significant vision in his right eye ​while in prison. "It's a very welcome order, and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much," ​PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari said. "He should remain in hospital until all ​doctors are satisfied," he said. The court has directed Khan be moved to Shifa ‌International ⁠Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16, Khan's spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha said on X. Since he lost power in a no-confidence vote, Khan has faced multiple cases, including over state ​gifts and an ​unlawful marriage. headlines.full_text: Trump to sign $5000 checks for all adults? POTUS makes big announcement ahead of midterms President Trump promises $5,000 checks to all adult citizens if Republicans win in the upcoming 2026 midterm elections. US PresidentDonald Trumphas once again enticed voters with a financial incentive ahead of November midterm elections. He announced that if Republicans win the House and the Senate he will issue $5,000 checks to all adult citizens in the United States. “If Republicans win theHouse of Representativesand theSenatein the 2026 Midterm Elections, I’m going to give all adult citizens in the United States of America, $5,000!” the POTUS announced. “Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I look forward to signing those checks!” he added. Trump maintained deliberately ambiguous eligibility criteria for the proposed dividend distribution, merely stipulating that all adult citizens would qualify. With approximately 245 million adult American citizens globally, the estimated fiscal obligation would reach $1.22 trillion. Trump clarified that the initiative would apply exclusively to adult citizens residing within the United States of America, potentially excluding roughly 2 million expatriate citizens who reside internationally while retaining American citizenship. Earlier, Senator Bernie Moreno announced on X that he would prepare legislation to enable Republicans to implement the Trump Dividend "immediately" should they achieve success in the midterm elections. headlines.full_text: Trump announces $90 checks for 20 million ‘wonderful’ people: Who are eligible for one-time payment? President Trump announced that over 20 million seniors will receive $90 checks this month to assist with Medicare premiums. PresidentDonald Trumpdeclared on Friday that more than 20 million "wonderful seniors" will get $90 checks this month to help with their Medicare premium payments. Seniors who qualify for Medicare Part B coverage will receive this one-time payment through either direct deposit or a mailed check, thanks to the Medicare Improvement Fund that was set up back in 2008, as per theWhite House. Trump described the Medicare Improvement Fund as “a pointless ‘Slush Fund’ that has only been used by Dumocrats in Congress to pay for the Waste, Fraud, and Abuse for their Special Interest friends, and drive up Healthcare costs.” “We are finally using this Fund, along with my Most Favored Nations Deals, to substantially LOWER costs for our Seniors,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. More than 20 million older Americans are expected to receive a one-time payment from Trump. Seniors whose Medicaid already covers their premiums or who pay an Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount won't be eligible. “I pledged to protect and preserve Medicare andSocial Security, which were on the verge of RUIN byJoe Biden, who foolishly and maliciously let tens of millions of Illegal Aliens into our Country, and we are doing just that for America’s Seniors,” Trump said.
